idea_text: MDP 里不同形式的不确定性是否等价

interpretations.description: Same hidden reward parameter, fixed per episode (A) vs redrawn i.i.d. per step (B); compare optimal values under the same history-dependent policy class.
information_conditions: information_available_to_policy: own actions and rewards, identical in A and B
working_assumptions: policy_class: deterministic history-dependent (randomised cannot do better)

interpretations.description: Bayesian (expected) vs robust (worst-case) treatment of the same uncertainty set.
information_conditions: decision_objective differs: expectation vs worst case

interpretations.description: All forms of MDP uncertainty are equivalent.
interpretations.rejection_reason: no uncertainty object, policy class or equivalence_definition is fixed; not testable as stated

open_items: Which equivalence notion is intended: equal optimal value, same optimal policy, or the same decision problem?
Is the comparison under expected return or worst-case return?

metrics: optimal value under a fixed policy class
field_problems.problem: When does persistent parameter uncertainty make history valuable?
When do robust (worst-case) formulations reduce to per-step games?
When can per-step randomness be marginalised into an ordinary MDP?
